name: frontend-design
description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building a new UI or reshaping an existing one.
about: Pushes the agent to choose a clear aesthetic direction, typography and layout for the real subject instead of templated defaults. It plans the design first, then builds it.
use_when: You are building a new UI or reshaping an existing one.
example: Redesign the home page of my blog so it does not look like a template.
author: Anthropic

name: web-artifacts-builder
description: Tools for building multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts with React, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui.
about: Includes scripts to start a frontend project and to bundle it into a single HTML artifact. Made for claude.ai artifacts, so it is most useful there.
use_when: You need an artifact with state management, routing or shadcn/ui components. Not for simple single-file pages.
example: Build a multi-page dashboard artifact with React and shadcn/ui.
author: Anthropic

name: theme-factory
description: Styles slides, docs, reports and HTML pages with one of 10 preset themes, or a new theme made on the fly.
about: Each theme is a set of colors and fonts. You pick one and the agent applies it to the artifact it already made.
use_when: You want consistent styling on a deck, document, report or landing page.
example: Apply one of the preset themes to this slide deck.
author: Anthropic

name: webapp-testing
description: Test local web apps with Playwright: verify frontend behavior, debug the UI, capture screenshots and read browser logs.
about: The agent writes native Python Playwright scripts. A helper script starts and stops the dev servers for you.
use_when: You want to check that a local web app works, or see why the UI misbehaves.
example: Open http://localhost:8080, fill in the signup form and take a screenshot.
author: Anthropic

name: mcp-builder
description: Guide for building high-quality MCP servers that let an LLM use an external service through well-designed tools.
about: Walks through four phases of building an MCP server, in Python (FastMCP) or Node/TypeScript (MCP SDK), and includes an evaluation script.
use_when: You are building an MCP server to connect an API or service.
example: Help me build an MCP server for the GitHub API in TypeScript.
author: Anthropic

name: skill-creator
description: Create new skills, improve existing ones and measure how reliably they trigger.
about: Covers writing a skill, running evals against it and benchmarking it. It ships scripts to validate and package a skill.
use_when: You want to create, edit or optimize a skill, or test whether its description triggers correctly.
example: Create a skill that drafts release notes from git commits.
author: Anthropic

name: internal-comms
description: Resources for writing internal communications: status reports, leadership updates, newsletters, FAQs and incident reports.
about: Includes formats such as 3P updates (Progress, Plans, Problems) so the writing follows a known structure.
use_when: You are asked for any kind of internal communication.
example: Write a 3P update for my team for this week.
author: Anthropic

name: test-driven-development
description: Write the test first, watch it fail, then write the minimum code to make it pass.
about: Enforces the red-green cycle. The skill's core rule: if you did not watch the test fail, you do not know it tests the right thing.
use_when: You are implementing a feature or a bug fix, before writing the implementation.
example: Add a slugify function using test-driven development.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: systematic-debugging
description: Find the root cause before proposing a fix, for any bug, failing test or unexpected behavior.
about: A step-by-step process whose first rule is that symptom fixes are failures. It also ships a script to find which test pollutes the others.
use_when: You hit a bug, a test failure or unexpected behavior.
example: The login test fails intermittently. Find the root cause.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: requesting-code-review
description: Dispatch a reviewer subagent with precisely crafted context to catch problems before they cascade.
about: The reviewer gets only the context it needs for the evaluation, not your whole session history.
use_when: You finished a task or a major feature, or you are about to merge.
example: Review my changes before I merge.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: receiving-code-review
description: Evaluate review feedback technically before implementing it, instead of agreeing by reflex.
about: Verify before implementing, ask before assuming. Useful when feedback is unclear or questionable.
use_when: You receive review feedback and have not acted on it yet.
example: Here is the reviewer's feedback. Decide which parts to apply and why.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: using-git-worktrees
description: Make sure feature work happens in an isolated workspace, with native worktree tools first and git worktree as a fallback.
about: Checks whether you are already isolated, then uses the platform's own tools, and only then plain `git worktree`.
use_when: You start feature work that should not touch the current workspace.
example: Start the new search feature in an isolated worktree.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: brainstorming
description: Find out what the user actually wants, and why, before any creative work or new feature.
about: The skill assumes the agent's idea of what you want is thinner than it feels, and asks first. It includes a small server for visual companion pages.
use_when: Before creating features, building components or planning anything new.
example: I want to add comments to my blog. Help me think it through first.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: writing-plans
description: Write an implementation plan detailed enough for an engineer who has not seen the codebase or the spec.
about: Turns a spec into a multi-step plan before any code is touched.
use_when: You have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task.
example: Write the implementation plan for the spec in docs/spec.md.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: verification-before-completion
description: Run the verification commands and read the output before claiming work is done, fixed or passing.
about: Core principle: evidence before claims. The agent must confirm with a command, not assume.
use_when: The agent is about to say work is complete, before committing or opening a PR.
example: Is this fixed? Verify before you say it is.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: writing-skills
description: Write and verify skills the way you write code: test scenarios first, then the skill.
about: Applies test-driven development to documentation: pressure scenarios with subagents, watch them fail, write the skill, watch them pass.
use_when: You create or edit a skill, or check that one works before you deploy it.
example: Write a skill that reviews pull requests, and test it.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: dispatching-parallel-agents
description: Give each of two or more independent problems to its own agent so they work at the same time.
about: Each agent gets isolated, precisely crafted context. Best for unrelated failures in different files or subsystems.
use_when: You face 2 or more tasks with no shared state and no required order.
example: These three test files fail for different reasons. Fix them in parallel.
author: Jesse Vincent

name: git-guardrails-claude-code
description: Set up Claude Code hooks that block dangerous git commands (push, reset --hard, clean, branch -D) before they run.
about: Installs a PreToolUse hook with a shell script. It works in Claude Code only, because it uses Claude Code hooks.
use_when: You want to prevent destructive git operations by the agent.
example: Block git push and reset --hard in Claude Code.
author: Matt Pocock

name: grilling
description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan, decision or idea, in rounds of numbered questions.
about: Maps the plan as a decision tree. Each round asks every question whose prerequisites are settled and gives a recommended answer for each.
use_when: You want to stress-test your thinking.
example: Grill me about my plan to move the blog to a new host.
author: Matt Pocock

name: handoff
description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
about: Saves a summary to a temp file, links to specs and commits instead of copying them, and suggests which skills the next agent should use.
use_when: You want a fresh agent to continue the work.
example: Write a handoff for the next agent.
author: Matt Pocock

name: setup-pre-commit
description: Set up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking and tests in the current repo.
about: Adds commit-time formatting, type checking and tests to a JavaScript or TypeScript project.
use_when: You want pre-commit hooks, Husky or lint-staged.
example: Set up Husky with lint-staged in this repo.
author: Matt Pocock

name: seo-audit
description: Audit a site for SEO problems: technical SEO, on-page SEO, meta tags, indexing and Core Web Vitals.
about: Diagnoses why a site is not ranking or lost traffic and gives actionable recommendations. It can read a product-marketing context file if you have one.
use_when: You ask for an SEO audit, or why you are not ranking.
example: Run an SEO audit on my blog.
author: Corey Haines

name: copywriting
description: Write or rewrite marketing copy for homepages, landing pages, pricing, feature and about pages.
about: Written as an expert conversion copywriter. It also checks for a product-marketing context file first.
use_when: You ask for new copy, a rewrite, a headline or CTA help.
example: Rewrite the hero copy of my landing page.
author: Corey Haines

name: cro
description: Analyze marketing pages and forms and recommend changes that raise conversion.
about: Starts with a page analysis, then loads reference guides for the area it recommends changes in.
use_when: A page or form is not converting.
example: Why isn't my landing page converting?
author: Corey Haines
